title: Computability theory: remaining extensions and research branches
area_fit: The pending branches extend finite approximation, computably enumerable constructions and oracle degrees. Develop bounded changes before more elaborate approximation classes, and introduce low sets before low constructions or a low-basis theorem. Keep these developments within ordinary computability unless a separate cross-area interface is planned.
reading_order_rule: Preserve the current dependency-respecting sequence. For any future execution, first select and fully inspect the indicated source material, check current human and formal prerequisites, then choose concrete entry scopes and placement. Local expansions retain their explicit placements below. The research branches are not ready-made batches.

pending_local_expansions.scope: Prove every infinite c.e. set has a total computable injective enumeration by suppressing repeated outputs; distinguish this from increasing enumeration and retain the finite-set obstruction.

State explicitly that ordinary first-order satisfiability with effective syntax and unrestricted model sizes is co-c.e., using proof enumeration of negations and a malformed-code test; no finite-satisfiability claim.

later_research_branches.topic: Bounded changes of mind and differences of c.e. sets
later_research_branches.scope: Develop the d.c.e. case before n-c.e. and computably bounded change counts. Fix the initial-bit and number-of-changes conventions. Infinite pointwise finite change does not supply a computable change bound.
later_research_branches.source_leads: Miller §40 Exercise 40.5(b) gives a difference-class application, only located here; select and fully inspect a source for the actual finite-mind-change theorem and any strictness claims before making an entry handoff.

later_research_branches.topic: Low sets and a low simple c.e. set
later_research_branches.scope: Define low by A-prime Turing equivalent to zero-prime, explain why an undecidable low c.e. set is incomplete, then construct one with a fully specified jump-restraint strategy.
later_research_branches.source_leads: Miller §29 Theorem 29.1, pp.58–60; statement and beginning of strategy located, not a full construction audit.

later_research_branches.scope: Keep splitting into noncomputable c.e. pieces separate from the stronger degree-splitting result. Do not infer incomparability or strict degree bounds from disjointness alone.
later_research_branches.source_leads: Miller §§30–31, pp.61–67, located by contents; full strategy and verification audits remain.

later_research_branches.topic: Low basis for effectively closed classes
later_research_branches.scope: After introducing low sets, construct a low member of a nonempty effectively closed binary class, with nested-tree compactness and the uniform halting-oracle choice proved.
later_research_branches.source_leads: Miller §46 Proposition 46.5, p.137, selected statement and short proof inspected as a research lead; translate its finite-oracle semantics and index uniformity explicitly before selecting it for drafting. The adjacent countable-path proposition needs the nonemptiness repair MILLER-CT-01.

later_research_branches.topic: Uniform oracle padding, fixed points, and complete-set isomorphisms at higher levels
later_research_branches.scope: Prove ordinary computable transformations valid for every supplied oracle before extending the ordinary complete-set permutation theorem to all positive hierarchy levels. Do not cite separate fixed-oracle existence statements as a uniform compiler.
later_research_branches.source_leads: Marks §15.1 Exercise 15.3 and the general §17.1 Lemma 17.1/Corollary 17.3; statements and argument inspected, but the missing all-oracle interfaces need their own coherent entry scope.

coverage_boundary: Genericity and forcing, density, jump inversion, minimal degrees, randomness, algorithmic information, hyperarithmetic theory and reverse mathematics remain later specialist development. Alternative lambda-calculus models and standard word, tiling and Post correspondence applications are optional separate branches. Effective model theory needs a cross-area interface plan. Resource complexity belongs in a separate area; Hilbert’s tenth problem needs substantial number theory.
execution_and_ownership: Future entry creation uses prompts01–06: root selects concrete scopes and source support before delegating entry pipelines, maintains reading order and shared integration, and coordinates independent reviews and writing builds.
source_limits: The research leads below do not constitute completed construction or formal-interface audits. Select their exact passages and resolve each stated source or uniformity limitation before drafting; consult the permanent source-error register for existing scoped findings.
